messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- [2025-11-06] handover/2025-11-06-feature-flags: Quick one: feature-flags belongs to team Ember starting today. Thanks to team Atlas for running it until now.
- [2026-02-11] handover/2026-02-11-feature-flags: The Ember team handed the flags service to the Dune team today; Oskar wrote up the handover doc for Farah.
- [2025-09-02] standup/atlas/2025-09-02: Decided in today's standup: clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds, since feature-flags saw 40,000 requests per second at peak and most of them were identical.
- [2025-01-08] standup/atlas/2025-01-08-2: The billing API lives with the Atlas team. For the record, feature-flags is owned by Atlas.
- [2025-04-24] standup/cinder/2025-04-24-2: Heads-up from the Cinder team: feature-flags' p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy.
- [2026-03-09] handover/2026-03-09-feature-flags-correction: Correction to the handover note of 2026-02-11: the flags service went to team Atlas, not Dune. Dune never owned it; the note was written against the wrong team.
- [2025-09-30] standup/atlas/2025-09-30: Decision: billing-api will gate the new invoice flow behind feature-flags, because the rollout needs a per-tenant kill switch. The billing API now depends on the feature flag service. The Atlas team planning meeting is every Tuesday.
- [2025-02-07] standup/ember/2025-02-07: Dependency map update: scheduler needs the feature flag service (per-job kill switches).
- [2025-12-31] standup/atlas/2025-12-31: Atlas saw that the feature flag service's queue depth hit 50,000 following the marketing send; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2025-04-29] standup/ember/2025-04-29: The scheduler still relies on the feature flag service; keep that in mind for the maintenance.
- [2026-02-03] standup/atlas/2026-02-03: The Atlas team now does a no-deploy Friday.
- [2025-05-07] standup/boreal/2025-05-07-2: The Boreal team noticed that the authentication gateway's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump and pinged the owners.
- [2025-07-29] standup/ember/2025-07-29: Policy: every auth-gateway change requires two reviewer approvals and a security sign-off.
- [2025-01-09] standup/boreal/2025-01-09-3: For the record, the webhook dispatcher is owned by team Boreal.
- [2025-05-14] standup/cinder/2025-05-14-2: Cinder adopted trunk-based development.
- [2025-01-09] standup/boreal/2025-01-09-2: The Boreal team owns the notifier.
- [2025-02-18] standup/ember/2025-02-18: Per the change policy, auth-gateway deploys on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.
- [2025-03-20] handover/2025-03-20-image-resizer: Ownership change: the image resizer now sits with team Ember. Team Dune no longer owns it.
- [2025-02-06] standup/ember/2025-02-06-2: Team Ember now does pairing on every production change.
- [2026-05-22] standup/dune/2026-05-22-3: Heads-up from the Dune team: the scheduler's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump.
- [2025-12-01] standup/boreal/2025-12-01-2: Boreal saw that the job scheduler's cold start time tripled following the runtime upgrade; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2025-03-20] standup/dune/2025-03-20: Reminder: the reports pipeline is owned by Dune.
- [2025-01-17] standup/cinder/2025-01-17: Team Cinder owns the product catalog.
- [2026-04-16] standup/atlas/2026-04-16: The Atlas team saw that the ledger service's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2025-09-05] standup/dune/2025-09-05: The Dune team still owns the scheduler, in case anyone asks.
- [2025-11-04] standup/ember/2025-11-04: The Ember team saw that the billing service's queue depth hit 50,000 following the marketing send; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2026-04-14] standup/dune/2026-04-14-3: Release captain for Q3 2025: Farah.
- [2025-05-22] standup/boreal/2025-05-22: Lena Fischer is the release captain for Q1 2026.
- [2026-04-13] standup/ember/2026-04-13-2: Ember still owns the reporting service, in case anyone asks.
- [2025-11-26] handover/2025-11-26-image-resizer: The Atlas team is taking over the image resizer from the Ember team, effective today. Dashboards and alerts are being repointed.
- [2025-01-20] standup/dune/2025-01-20: The Dune team owns the image resizer.
- [2026-05-22] standup/dune/2026-05-22-2: The Dune team noticed that auth-gateway's CPU sat at 90 percent after the traffic shift and pinged the owners.
- [2025-11-03] standup/boreal/2025-11-03-2: Heads-up from the Boreal team: the notification service's CPU sat at 90 percent after the traffic shift.
- [2025-01-20] standup/ember/2025-01-20: The job scheduler lives with the Ember team. For the record, the authentication gateway is owned by Ember.

Question: As of now, which team is responsible for feature-flags?
